channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest Brussels posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: Man held two teenage boys as 'real slaves' in Brussels flat as their father lay dying
item.description: A 25-year-old man accused of violence against teenagers, neighbours and former partners allegedly terrorised residents of a Molenbeek building for nearly two years.

item.title: Students protest in Brussels against an increase in tuition fees
item.description: Hundreds of students from French-speaking higher education institutions marched through central Brussels on Wednesday to protest against the rising cost of student life

item.title: Far-right MP freed after being stuck in Flemish Parliament toilet for 13 hours
item.description: Vlaams Belang MP Frédéric Erens was freed by emergency services after a defective lock left him trapped in a toilet at the Flemish Parliament for nearly 13 hours.

item.title: Major traffic disruptions expected in Brussels as student protest against reforms on Wednesday
item.description: Police are warning of major traffic disruption in and around Brussels' city centre.

item.title: Brussels' debt could become three times as large as its revenue in five years
item.description: How broke are the regions and communities in Belgium? And how easily could they dig themselves out of a financial hole in the future?

item.title: Drive baby drive: How Brussels traffic drives everyone mad
item.description: "You have the cars, which have been here for generations, taking up all the space they need. And then you have the invasive species – the bikes, scooters, joggers and pedestrians – all trying to grab a share of the space."

item.title: Brussels' Kanal Museum announces free opening weekend - Reservations open
item.description: Brussels' new museum of modern and contemporary art, Kanal, will open on Saturday 28 November.

item.title: Man who stole luxury watches from high-end gyms arrested in Brussels
item.description: A suspect linked to several thefts of luxury watches and jewellery from sports clubs across Belgium was arrested after being recognised by a club manager in Woluwe-Saint-Lambert.

item.title: Brussels casino workers seek clarity as 286 jobs hang in balance
item.description: The workers called on the City of Brussels mayor to provide clarity about the casino's status before its current concession expires at the end of 2026.

item.title: 'A safer space': Green light for major redesign of Place Bethléem in Saint-Gilles
item.description: "By making public spaces more attractive and of higher quality, we want to ensure that local residents can once again fully reclaim those spaces."

item.title: Belgian man shot in brutal robbery in Ecuador
item.description: Followed and cornered by several perpetrators in a car, a Belgian man was violently robbed in the port city of Guayaquil in Ecuador.

item.title: Brussels Airport 'experience of the future' clashes with Paris Agreement
item.description: The expansion of Brussels Airport clashes with the Paris Climate Agreement, according to an examination by sustainability NGO Transport & Environment.

item.title: Interior Minister wants to expand army patrols to Brussels’ drugs hotspots
item.description: "As far as I know, this is the first time there has been an attack on a police station," says Quintin. "That’s worrying, but I see it as a sign that our approach is working."

item.title: Large-scale search operation for KU Leuven professor missing in Scottish Highlands
item.description: A priest, hiker, and Bible studies professor at KU Leuven has been missing since Sunday morning in the Scottish Highlands.

item.title: Alleged hit squad that sprayed 15 bullets into wrong home faces trial
item.description: It is believed that the perpetrators accidentally attacked the home of an unsuspecting family whose surname differed from the intended target by only one letter.

item.title: Woman buried husband in family's backyard and continued to live there for eight years
item.description: The remains of Farid B. who disappeared in 2018, were found beneath the family's concrete terrace in Visé, where his partner and their son had continued to live for eight years.

item.title: Soaring tuition fees push students to rely on part-time jobs to pay for studies
item.description: Students in French-speaking Belgium are relying on part-time jobs to cover the cost of their studies as the latest education reform pushes fees higher.

item.title: Two women dead after incident in Anderlecht
item.description: Two women were found dead on Sunday in Avenue de la Poésie in Anderlecht, and prosecutors are treating the deaths as suspicious.

item.title: Brussels families join lawsuit against harmful flight path
item.description: Campaigners say more than 459,000 residents now live under a landing corridor affecting eight times more people than alternative routes.

item.title: Drone flying over Brussels Airport forces three flights to divert
item.description: Federal police have confirmed that an investigation to uncover the drone's operator is underway. There is apparently no clear indication that the incidents were the work of a criminal network or foreign power.
